datingPagesAClassBrings.note: When a class page is published, the pages it links to can take the class's date. Shared because the date is what ORDERS a page on the site, both apps write it, and the Python installer already follows the same convention when it pre-populates a course.

frontmatterKey.why: A page inside the section's own folder belongs to one section and carries 'created'. A course-level page is shared between sections and carries one key per section, so hiding or dating it for section 1 says nothing about section 2.

movesWhen: the page is reached by following links from a class page being published
the page is HIDDEN right now, so this publish is the first time students will see it
the page is not itself a class page
doesNotMoveWhen: the page is already visible to students - it has a place on the site somebody may have linked to or looked at, and republishing a class must not shuffle work that was already out
the page named for publishing is not a class page - there is no class day to inherit
the page is a class page - a class's date is its position in the schedule and nothing may move it

sharedPagesMoveToo.why: A page several classes link to still moves, as long as students have never seen it. An earlier rule left shared pages alone - 'a concept page linked from three different lessons belongs to none of them' - which is sound for a page already on the site and beside the point for one nobody can reach. A page students cannot see has no place to be left in; it has only the day its FILE was made, which is a fact about the teacher's evening rather than about the course.

whenSeveralClassesShareAPage.why: The same convention the course installer already uses - first_use_dates in setup_course.py dates a shared page to the first class that references it - so a pre-populated course and a hand-published one date their pages the same way. Ties are broken by page title so two classes on one day give the same answer every run rather than depending on folder order.

bothRoutesAgree.why: Naming the class ('publish Unit 2, Day 3') and naming its day ('publish tomorrow's class') are two ways of saying one thing and must date pages identically. They did not: the by-day route worked the dates out and the by-name route passed an empty list, so the same teacher got two different results depending on which sentence they used.

neverPublishedIsInferred.from: the page being hidden at the moment the publish is planned
neverPublishedIsInferred.why: Nothing on disk records a page's history. A page published once and later hidden therefore counts as never published and would take a new date. Recording the truth would mean a new frontmatter key on every page, agreed between both apps and the Python; the inference costs nothing and is right in every case anybody has met.

datingNonClassPages.note: Pages that are not linked from a Unit x, Day y page, and are not themselves a Unit x, Day y page (such as sidebar pages, Curriculum pages, and Key Links pages not referenced in any class lesson), inherit the same date as the first class of the year (Unit 1, Day 1) when a site is previewed or deployed, and upon course setup.
appliesTo: sidebar pages (e.g., folder index.md files — the section landing page carries its newest published class's date)
Key Links pages that are not linked from any Unit x, Day y class page
Curriculum pages (index, expectation notes, and unreferenced expectations)
standalone reference or utility pages not linked from any class page
datingNonClassPages.dateInherited: the date of Unit 1, Day 1 (or the earliest class of the year)
datingNonClassPages.why: Pages that serve the course as a whole belong to the start of the semester rather than carrying arbitrary install timestamps, changing build timestamps, or file creation times.

cases.name: renames run highest day first
cases.why: Working UP would try to make Day 2 into Day 3 while a real Day 3 is still called that: either it overwrites a lesson, or — with a never-overwrite guard — it silently skips, leaving two pages claiming to be Day 3. Working down means every destination has already been vacated.

cases.name: later units move their dates but are not renumbered
cases.why: Unit 2 Day 1 stays Unit 2 Day 1 — its number means something to the teacher. It is the DATE that shifts, because the new class takes a teaching day.

cases.name: a page named some other way is left where it is
cases.why: The trip keeps its date and its name, and the plan SAYS so before the teacher agrees — an unnumbered page silently keeping a date that everything around it moved off is the kind of thing noticed weeks later.

insertion.note: Making room for a class in the middle of a unit. The RENAME ORDER is the part to get right and the part that looks like an implementation detail: it is the difference between a course that survives and one that loses a lesson.

cases.why: A section with no numbered class at all starts at Unit 1, Day 1.
The highest UNIT wins, then the highest day within it — a new class belongs to the unit the teacher is currently in, not to whichever unit has the most days.

nextClass.note: What 'add the next class' would be called: the highest unit these pages name, and one past the highest day inside it.

note: Naming, numbering and making room for classes. All of it is pure rules over page titles and dates, so all of it is portable. The insertion cases are the highest-stakes data in these contracts: they rename files a teacher's lessons live in.

numberedClassOrder.note: Numbered pages sort by unit, then by day — not by date and not by filename.
numberedClassOrder.why: Day 10 after Day 2, so this cannot be a string sort. And 'Field Trip' is dropped from the list rather than sorted to one end.

cases.title: Unit 2 Day 4
cases.why: The comma is part of the form. Accepting near-misses means guessing at what a teacher meant by a name, and the cost of guessing wrong is a renamed lesson.

pageNaming.note: Which class-page titles carry numbers. A page named some other way — 'Field Trip', 'Exam Review' — is NOT guessed at: it is passed over everywhere classes are renumbered, and keeps its own date. The plan says how many were skipped so nobody is surprised.

refusals.note: Named by case, not by message: which refusal it is must match on both platforms, while the sentence a teacher reads is the product's wording.
